text.p: Percepio View is a free event tracing tool for embedded software, based on Percepio Tracealyzer, designed to help you inspect task execution and debug RTOS-related issues. Percepio View offers snapshot tracing and a core set of Tracealyzer views, streamlined for simplicity. For advanced features, including trace streaming and profiling support, consider upgrading to Percepio Profile or Percepio Tracealyzer.

Percepio View complements your classic debugger with graphical timeline of the software execution, including threads, RTOS API calls and other important events. Moreover, the support for User Event logging offers a superior alternative to traditional printf logging, with minimal overhead and with integrated display in the trace views. This means you can add a lot more logging without any significant impact on the system execution and timing.
Percepio View does not require additional tracing hardware, which means it can be used on essentially any target processor and can be used with many different development tools.

Percepio View consists of two main components:
The host-side application, that provide trace visualization and analysis. Percepio View runs on Microsoft Windows and Linux hosts. Instructions for Linux users are found here.
The TraceRecorder library. Read more under the Creating and Loading Traces section.

Percepio Profile is a powerful tool for tracing and visualization of embedded and IoT software systems at runtime. Inspect task execution, debug RTOS-related issues, and profile your system from multiple perspectives. With Percepio Profile you can record long traces by continuous trace streaming. Analyze task timing metrics, task communication flow, stack usage, heap usage, and visualize data plots for a comprehensive view of your system’s performance and behavior.

For even more powerful features, including user-defined profiling (e.g., custom intervals), advanced RTOS analytics, and additional trace streaming options, consider upgrading to Percepio Tracealyzer.

Percepio Profile complements your classic debugger with graphical timeline of the software execution, including threads, RTOS API calls and other important events. Moreover, the support for User Event logging offers a superior alternative to traditional printf logging, with minimal overhead and with integrated display in the trace views. This means you can add a lot more logging without any significant impact on the system execution and timing.

Percepio View is designed for use with SEGGER J-Link or J-Trace debug probes using the RTT protocol. This can be used with any processor supported by SEGGER J-Link and that allows background memory access while the target is running. This includes most Arm Cortex-M devices, as well as certain Arm Cortex-R, Arm Cortex-A and Renesas RX devices.

Percepio Profile consists of two main components:
The host-side application, that provide trace visualization and analysis. Percepio View runs on Microsoft Windows and Linux hosts. Instructions for Linux users are found here.
The TraceRecorder library. Read more under the Creating and Loading Traces section.

$PRODUCT is a powerful tool for tracing and visualization of embedded and IoT software systems at runtime. More than 30 views offers amazing insight into the real-time behavior, speeding up debugging, validation and performance optimization. This saves you many hours of frustrating trial-and-error troubleshooting. With $PNAME you see what is really going on in your system!

$PNAME provide state-of-the-art visualization developed since 2004 and actually understands the meaning of many software events from supported RTOSes and middleware stacks. This allows $PNAME to perform advanced analyses and provide many specialized visualizations, with intuitive links between the views and highlighting of related events. The resulting visualization makes it much easier to draw conclusions from the data, understand the problem and verify the solution.

For RTOS-based systems, $PNAME shows task scheduling and timing, calls to RTOS services (including blocking and timeouts) and internal RTOS events such as task activations and OS ticks. $PNAME can also show interrupt handlers as well as User Events logged from your application code.

On top of this, $PNAME allows you to create user-defined visualizations using State Machines and Custom Intervals. This way, you can visualize specific aspects of importance for your system and the problem at hand.

$PNAME can be used side-by-side with a traditional debugger and complements the debugger view with a higher level perspective, ideal for understanding real-time issues where a classic debugger is not sufficient.
$PNAME does not require additional tracing hardware, which means that it can be used in deployed systems to capture rare errors which otherwise are hard to reproduce.

$PRODUCT consists of two main components:
The host application $PNAME, that provide trace visualization and analysis. $PNAME runs on Microsoft Windows and Linux hosts. Instructions for Linux users are found in RunningOnLinux.txt in the $PNAME application directory.
A trace creation component. $PNAME supports several third-party solutions provided by RTOS vendors, and Percepio also provides the Percepio Trace Recorder library that supports several RTOSes and soon also bare-metal setups. Read more under the Creating and Loading Traces section.
An installation guide for Linux users is found at https://percepio.com/running-tracealyzer-on-linux/. Additional information is also found in RunningOnLinux.txt, found in the application directory.
Note that display scaling is not yet fully supported on Linux, so it is recommended to use 100% scale factor.
